## Disorder as a materials-design tool

I am a tenure-track Assistant Professor at École Polytechnique, where I study chemically complex and disordered inorganic materials.

My research combines solid-state synthesis, structural characterization and computational modelling to understand how configurational disorder influences phase stability, local structure and functional properties.

[Research](research.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [Publications](publications.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

::: {.hero-card}
### Current interests

- High-entropy and entropy-stabilized oxides
- Short-range order and local distortions
- Phase stability and order–disorder transitions
- First-principles and machine-learning methods
- Lead-free functional oxides
:::
:::

## Research approach

I work across experiment and computation, connecting synthesis and diffraction measurements with density-functional theory, statistical mechanics and machine-learning interatomic potentials.
